title: Financial Tools Access and Navigation (FinTAN)
official: Financial Tools Access and Navigation (FinTAN) for Supported Financial Decision Making
summary: The specific aims of this study are to: i) collaboratively create a Financial Tools Access and Navigation (FinTAN) guide to assist persons and care providers to identify the potential utility of relevant financial products, and guide them in their use; ii) pilot test the feasibility and impact of using the FinTAN guide and the associated financial tools and services among people with SMI and those who assist them with their money management; iii) prepare for a future full-scale clinical trial of the FinTAN guide and relevant financial tools and services. The goal for this research project is to create a guide that can assist in creating a Supported Financial Decision Making (SFDM) arrangements, whereby persons with SMI can access the support they need with their finances while maximizing autonomy and flexibility over time.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 years of age or older who are using services at the Connecticut Mental Health Center
* Self-identify as having money management challenges
* Provide services at the community mental health center
* Provide financial management support to people who have SMI

Exclusion Criteria:

* Vulnerable populations will not be recruited (ie prisoners, pregnant women, decisionally impaired).
